front.title: Open Action Record (OAR): Authority, Approval and Outcome Evidence for AI Agent Actions

abstract.t:
Several profiles record what an AI agent was asked to do, and the decision taken, as signed statements registered with a transparency service. Protocols for agent identity and delegated authorization say whether an agent may ask. After an incident or in a dispute, three further questions decide the case: were the authorizations the action relied on still valid when it committed, did a named person approve this exact action, and did the action change the system of record as recorded?
This document defines evidence that any agent action profile can add to answer them: an authority set that binds the digests of the outside authorizations an action relied on to that one action, with a re-check recorded at the moment it commits; an approval binding that ties a person's confirmation, by a passkey or an outside approval service, to the exact action and to what the person was shown; salted commitments to the affected state before and after execution; an outcome confirmation made by reading the system of record; and three outcome classes a relying party can act on. Values are hidden behind salted commitments and can be disclosed field by field. The constructions are implemented in the Open Action Record (OAR) format, with three verifiers that agree on published test vectors.
